title: Exchange transfusion in neonates (double-volume)
subject: paediatrics
summary: A double-volume exchange replaces 2 x the blood volume (100 mL/kg preterm, 85 mL/kg term), about 86% of the baby's blood. Use irradiated, cross-matched reconstituted blood with haematocrit 50 to 60% through an 8 Fr umbilical venous catheter, in aliquots of at most 5 mL/kg at no more than 2 mL/kg/minute over 1 to 2 hours, with phototherapy before, during and after.

sections.title: Indication
items: Decide on exchange using the thresholds in the Neonatal jaundice protocol. The procedure should be done by experienced staff with informed parental consent.

sections.title: Prepare
items: Use an open bed to prevent heat loss. Nil by mouth is not required; empty the stomach by nasogastric tube if needed. Have resuscitation equipment ready and monitor throughout.
Continue intensive phototherapy before, during and after the exchange.
Blood: the blood bank reconstitutes red cells and plasma to a haematocrit of 50 to 60%. With ABO incompatibility use group O red cells and AB plasma. Whole blood must be fresh (under 24 hours).
Without ABO incompatibility, saline or albumin can replace plasma, and blood of the baby's own group is used; in subgroup incompatibility use blood negative for the causative antigen.
Cross-match donor blood with the mother's blood for an urgent delivery room exchange or intrauterine transfusion, otherwise with the baby's blood. Irradiate, filter and warm the blood.

sections.title: Procedure
items: Access: umbilical venous catheter, 8 Fr recommended for exchange.

Volume: 2 x total blood volume, taking 100 mL/kg for preterm and 85 mL/kg for term babies (see the procedure calculator). This exchanges about 86% of the baby's blood. Plasma volume = exchange volume minus red cell volume.
Exchange at most 5 mL/kg at a time, no faster than 2 mL/kg/minute to avoid swings in blood pressure and intracranial pressure; the whole exchange takes 1 to 2 hours.
Alternative: synchronous peripheral arterial out, venous in, at 3 to 5 mL/min (one Chinese series, which also took neonatal blood volume as about 80 mL/kg).
Routine calcium infusion during the exchange is not recommended.

sections.title: Monitoring
items: Measure serum bilirubin within 2 hours of the procedure.
Check blood gas, glucose, electrolytes and calcium before and after; one series drew about 10 mL before and after for bilirubin, liver and renal function, gas, glucose and electrolytes.
The exchange removes drugs: repeat doses or monitor levels. Antibiotics are not needed afterwards unless infection is suspected.

sections.title: Complications
items: Apnoea, bradycardia, hypotension or hypertension, hypocalcaemia, hypo- or hyperglycaemia, hyperkalaemia, thrombocytopenia, neutropenia, coagulopathy, DIC, metabolic acidosis, vascular spasm, thrombosis, embolism, feeding intolerance, NEC, omphalitis and sepsis.
Mortality risk is about 1% in otherwise healthy and 12% in ill babies.
